paragraphs: Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana.

Hyman places him in Rava’s time, citing כב״א צא. (compare [Bava Kamma 91a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.91a.5)): Rava said …, and on this Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana, said: “This implies,” etc. In [Zevachim 55a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.55a.1-3), Hyman gives Rava bar Rav Chanan as teaching before Rava. In reply Rava cites what Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana, taught. Hyman next notes Abaye’s response.[^4]

Hyman calls him a master of the traditions (mara de-shema’ta), always mentioned in halakhic discussion: [Beitzah 7a](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.7a.16), [Sotah 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.30b.6), [Bava Kamma 23a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.23a.9), [23b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.23b.4-5) (and on this Mar Zutra objects), there [44b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.44b.1), [99a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.99a.7), [Bekhorot 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.12a.24), [33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.33b.3).

notes.text: The supplied כב״א צא. is irregular. Neither the checked Bava Batra 91a nor Bava Metzia 91a supplied the quoted Mari chain in this bounded check. The locator remains unresolved; the other quotations stay attributed to Hyman.

No new primary scalar was returned. Supplied כב״א צא. remains literal with work unresolved: the earlier bounded Bava Batra91a and Bava Metzia91a checks did not match the Mari chain. Neither finite miss proves absence elsewhere, and the old Bava Batra expansion is withdrawn in this new version. ר״כ expands locally to Rav Kahana from the full heading. ע״ז means ON THIS in both clauses, not Avodah Zarah. Rava’s statement and Mari’s inference are separate; Mar Zutra raises the later objection. All cited sides, bare Bava Kamma99 without an added side, dashes and etc. remain. Hyman’s ALWAYS-mentioned characterization is attributed, not new corpus coverage.

The dialogue is found in Bava Kamma 90b–91a. Rava reports a discussion that continues across the page break, and Rav Mari son of Rav Kahana subsequently says “This implies” about the proceeds of renting out an ox to plow. Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 906) has the irregular locator כב״א צא., retained here alongside the identified passage. In Zevachim 55a the consulted reading is Rabbah bar Rav Chanan before Rava; the print in Hyman has Rava bar Rav Chanan. The Mari passages at the other named loci are legal discussions. Mar Zutra’s objection is on 23b, and the bare reference 99 matches 99a in the consulted text.

[Zevachim 55a:1–3](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.55a.1-3) gives Rabbah bar Rav Chanan where Hyman gives Rava bar Rav Chanan. Rav Mari’s teaching is cited in the exchange. [Seder HaDorot 2399](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2399&lang=en) lists several of these same legal passages but questions a different teacher association attributed to She’erit Yosef.
